sentence: This project builds patient-derived xenograft models from patient populations so cancer research better represents the patients a cancer center serves.
This project studies how a protein that binds RNA helps hepatocellular carcinoma cells spread and affects endothelial cells, using cell, animal, and human specimen studies.
This project tests whether antagonist antibodies bring more immune cells into tumors and help T cells work there, and whether angiogenesis inhibitors add to this.
This project studies in mouse models of glioblastoma whether an existing memory immune response to an injected oncolytic virus helps the tumor get rejected.
This project builds a genetic screening platform that tests genes and mutations in combination to study how cell fate specification works.
This project develops a strategy that targets apoptotic cells to make radiotherapy work better for cancer treatment.
This project develops an immunotherapy for lung cancer using T cells engineered with a T cell receptor that targets a cancer-testis antigen.
This project looks at the biology of stress and social determinants of health in relation to cancer disparities.
This project uses machine learning on genomic data to study genetic links between childhood cancers and structural birth defects.
This project tests whether a form of the medication carvedilol can protect skin from radiation damage and skin cancer.
This project engineers human glial cells that help repair injuries to the central nervous system.
This project studies how acute myeloid leukemia cells use niches in the bone marrow to avoid chemotherapy, using spatial omic technologies.
This project collects and shares brains and biospecimens, and uses whole slide imaging with machine learning and postmortem imaging in neuropathology research.
This project runs a clinical research center that joins multi-center clinical trials on safe and effective ways to treat and prevent food allergy.
This project develops a method that uses nanobodies to remove or track retrotransposon proteins in cells and study their effects on health and disease.
This project builds data resources and artificial intelligence tools to help toxicological laboratories identify known and unknown designer drugs.
This project studies the molecular pathways that cause trabecular meshwork dysfunction and raise intraocular pressure in glaucoma.
This project uses machine learning on RNA and genome sequences to find genetic causes of hypoplastic left heart syndrome.
This project builds a data repository that collects, stores, and shares theranostics images and clinical information for prostate cancer and neuroendocrine tumors.
This project uses electronic health records and computational linguistic methods to build models that predict unplanned readmission of patients with psychosis.
